question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13{x}_{2} &=13 \\ {x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=3 \\ -{x}_{1}+4(1) &=3 \\ -{x}_{1} &=-1 \\ {x}_{1} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=5 \\ 5(1)+2(1) &=5 \\ 7 &=5\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13{x}_{2} &=13 \\ {x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=3 \\ -{x}_{1}+4(1) &=3 \\ -{x}_{1} &=-1 \\ {x}_{1} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=7 \\ 5(1)+2(1) &=7 \\ 7 &=7\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=1$, which means

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(1)+(1)=2.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=4\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=4$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=1 \\ (4)-{x}_{2} &=1 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-3 \\ {x}_{2} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3$, which means

$$
4{c}_{1}+3{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(4)+(3)=7.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ -59/2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ -59/2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1} \\ 7{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ -59/2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -31 \\ -59/2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-31 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{59}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $-2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1} &=-3 \\ {x}_{1} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 5(1)+2{x}_{2} &=-14 \\ 2{x}_{2} &=-19 \\ {x}_{2} &=- \frac{19}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{19}{2}$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{59}{2} \\ -(1)+3\left(- \frac{19}{2}\right) &=- \frac{59}{2} \\ - \frac{59}{2} &=- \frac{59}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{19}{2}$, which means

$$
{a}_{1}-19/2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(1)+\left(- \frac{19}{2}\right)=- \frac{17}{2}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8(2) &=-1 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=15 \\ {x}_{1} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ -2(5)+4(2) &=-2 \\ -2 &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=2$, which means

$$
5{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(5)+(2)=7.
$$
